title: Break Problems into Smaller Tasks
learningObjectives: Describe problem decomposition and its purpose.
Identify major responsibilities in a larger problem.
Split tasks into coherent, testable subtasks.
Recognize dependencies and arrange task order.
Review subtasks for clarity and unnecessary fragmentation.

understand.concept: Problem decomposition divides a complex goal into manageable tasks with clear responsibilities and outputs. Tasks should be sized sensibly, dependencies identified, and work ordered before combining the parts.
understand.whyItMatters: Smaller tasks reduce cognitive load, reveal missing work, and simplify testing, debugging, and collaboration.
understand.analogy: Preparing a meal by separating preparation, cooking, serving, and cleanup.
understand.analogyLimit: Over-decomposition adds overhead; stop when each task is understandable and manageable.

explain.narrative: Start with the main goal, identify responsibilities, split unclear parts, define each task's inputs and outputs, arrange dependencies, and verify both individual tasks and the combined solution.
